bridge_candidates.bridge_abstraction: Use searchable certificates as the carrier instead of advised hard truth tables, so that uniform search rather than nonuniform choice selects the hard slice.

falsifiers: Accepted pairs exist only through advice or nonuniform selection.
Certificate length or verifier time becomes m^{1+Omega(1)} in the exponent and leaves E.
The accepted certificate set is dense, polynomial-time decidable, and useful, triggering natural-proof pressure.
bridge_candidates.paper_safe_narrative: The proposed abstraction shifts attention from hard truth tables to uniformly searchable certificates of hardness, making advice leakage and naturalness the central tests.
bridge_candidates.preserved_invariant: uniform construction of the target language, no advice-selected hard strings, and exact worst-case lower-bound soundness
bridge_candidates.proof_obligation: Show that accepted certificate pairs exist in every kappa-gap interval, have O(m)-bit descriptions, are searchable in 2^{O(m)}, and soundly imply CC(f_u)>2^{epsilon m}.

falsifiers: The property is dense and decidable in polynomial time over truth tables.

The sparse slice has no transfer certificate back to the target theorem.

bridge_candidates.preserved_invariant: usefulness against the target circuit class without claiming a large constructive property
bridge_candidates.proof_obligation: Prove either non-largeness, nonconstructivity, or a proof-mediated escape while retaining a formal implication from property membership to target lower bound.
